To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the body and its internal organs change during lactation in a way that depends partly on the species and partly on the nutritional state of the lactating female.

(i) lactation is a demanding period for the mother's body; (ii) lactation is accompanied by a considerable increase in food intake; (iii) the increase in food intake is partly due to an increase in the size of the gastrointestinal tract; (iv) the liver also increases considerably during lactation and this is due partly to an increase in cell number; (v) lactation is followed by a decrease in the size of both the liver and the gastrointestinal tract.
the body and its various organs undergo considerable changes during lactation, and that the changes vary with the species, the diet and the duration of lactation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of lactation on the body and its components, especially the liver, and with the effects of the changes on the metabolism of the lactating female.
the following questions: How much food do lactating animals eat?
the changes in the composition of body tissues during lactation in the rat, and with the effects of these changes on subsequent fertility and lactation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lactation makes considerable demands on the mother and that these demands are met partly by mobilizing the mother's body and partly by an increase in the food intake.
the changes in the body and organs of lactating animals are not yet sufficiently understood, nor is their significance for the nutrition of the young known.
lactation in rats and probably in women leads to a loss of body fat, a loss of calcium and a possible loss of protein, depending on the diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nutritional requirements of the mother during lactation depend on how much of the milk is produced by the mother's body and how much she takes in with the food.
the body changes that occur during lactation are a reflection of the demands of the mother's milk on her metabolism and that they are reversible.
the body changes which take place during pregnancy and lactation are not only interesting from the biological point of view, but may also be important in the nutrition of the lactating mother.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gut microbiome is a key driver of lactation performance and the ability to produce milk, said senior author Justin Sonnenburg, PhD, associate professor of microbiology and immunology at Stanford University School of Medicine.
there are a variety of changes in the body during lactation, some of which are reversible and some not.
the gut microbiome can change rapidly in response to dietary interventions, and that these changes can be sustained for a long time after the intervention has ended.
